column2: Those always bent on finding faults and set to trouble us — may they all, struck by the sound of Kartavirya's great conch,
suddenly vanish, bewildered, as if from afar. The demons, great Adityas, Yakshas and Rakshasas,
Pishachas of great strength, spirits and Brahma-demons, planets of epilepsy and the flesh-eating planets,
drinkers of great blood, Vetalas and Guhyakas, Gandharvas, Apsaras, Siddhas and those born as gods and the like,
Dakinis, Drunasas, ghosts, field-guardians, Vinayakas, great tigers, great clouds, those of the form of great horses,
great elephants, great lions, great buffalo-born, bear, boar, dog, monkey and owl forms,
those with heads of great camel, donkey, cat, serpent, cow and bull, of various forms, of great strength, giving thousands of various troubles,
causing various diseases, petty or of great vigour and strength, windy, bilious, dreadful, phlegmatic and mixed ones,
the great planets of Maheshvara, of Vishnu, of Brahma, of Skanda, of Vinayaka, cruel ones, Pramathas and Guhyakas,
slayers of great enemies, fierce, great plague and smallpox, one-day, two-day, three-day great fevers,
four-day, fortnightly, monthly and six-monthly ones, yearly fevers hard to avert, supremely dreadful,
the great portents in dreams and the planets of bad dreams, Kushmandas, Jrimbhikas, earth spirits, Dronas, those who cheat by their nearness,
giddiness-causers, takers of life, child-planets and the rest, great planets that take away mind, intellect and senses, and pustules,
great eaters, eaters of offerings, eaters of great carrion, day-wanderers, night-wanderers, those dreadful at twilights,
whether negligent or careful, who are set to trouble me — may all those, struck by arrows shot from Kartavirya's bow,
be destroyed in a thousand ways, their strength and effort broken. The serpents, the great nagas, dwellers in the holes of great mountains,
black snakes, of great fangs, those called great pythons, Ananta, Shulika and others, with fangs and poison of great terror,
with hundreds of heads, with severed tails, dreadful; great poisonous leeches, scorpions with red tails,
Ashivisha, Kalakuta, the one named Mahahalahala, water-snakes, water-reptiles, crocodiles, tortoises,
fish with poisonous tails and other water-dwellers, water-born and land-born and artificial, of great poison,
hidden-formed with hidden poison, mice, house lizards, various dreadful ones, and those named great sub-poisons,
who wish to harm us, destroyers of body and life — may all those, split by Kartavirya's thousand swords,
perish from afar, their senses and strength lost. Men, animals, bears, monkeys, forest-roamers,
lions, tigers, boars, buffalo, great beasts, elephants, horses, gayals, asses, sharabhas, wolves,
dogs, leopards, white cats greedy for holes, jackals, hares, hawks, Garuda-like birds,
bheruṇḍas, crows, vultures, swans and the other classes of birds; sprout-born, egg-born, sweat-born and womb-born,
born of various kinds, of various separate types, who wish to harm us, by day and night in the ...
may all those, split by Kartavirya's thousand maces, perish from afar, their motion and manliness gone.
Those who give misfortune and those who practise deceit and illusion, who cause killing, uprooting, hatred and bewilderment,
destroyers of trust, the wicked, those who betray their master, assailants, the evil, the sinful who steal secrets,
givers of great pain by burning, harm, poison and fall of weapons, givers of fear by seizing fields and wealth, by binding and the like,
calamities of various forms (locusts, rats and the like), and other wicked species, those who trouble always and seek an opening to harm —
may all those, split by Kartavirya's thousand discuses, perish from afar, their strength and daring destroyed.
The clouds, the great rains, the winds, the lightnings, the bright great thunderbolts, the dreadful crashes,
the dreadful falls of meteors, the rainbow and the like; the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn,
Rahu and the dreadful Ketus, the stars and the signs, the tithis, transits, months, half-years, the leaders of the ages,
the lords of Manvantaras, Siddhas, sages, yoga-successes, treasures, the Rik, Yajus, Sama and Atharva, the fires,
seasons, guardians of the worlds, the ancestors, the assembly of gods, the sixty-four kinds of science in the three worlds —
all those mentioned here and those not mentioned, may they always be gentle to us, bringing happiness at all times.
By the command of Kartavirya, lord of yogis, of immeasurable splendour: Kartavirya Arjuna the archer, king of kings, lord of the Haihayas,
destroyer of the pride of the ten-faced (Ravana), proud of playing in the Reva (Narmada), very hard to conquer, remover of sorrow, subduer of thieves, king of kings, lord,
all-knowing, all-giving, glorious, giver of all desired by the good, accomplished, crest-jewel of kings, yogi, lord of the seven continents,
victorious, conqueror of the universe, eloquent, of great course, free of greed, sacrificer, fond of Brahmins, learned, to be known by Brahmins, eternal,
lord of Mahishmati, warrior, of great fame, of great arms, gentle, great hero, slayer of epidemics, intoxicated-eyed,
Shatrughna, eternal, brave, bearer of the conch, beloved of yogis, great devotee of Bhagavan, wise, destroyer of great fear,
invincible, divine in form, a state pervading the three worlds, victor over senses, victor over enemies, self-willed, of infinite valour,
discus-bearer, destroyer of enemy circles, honoured in the rules of battle, bearer of all scriptures and arts, stainless, honoured by the world,
hero rich in stainless goodness, of great strength and valour, honoured by victory and prosperity, conqueror of foes, leader of mantras,
sword-bearer, wish-giver, lovely, slayer of time, lotus-eyed, fond of auspicious talk, physician, wise, boon-giver, self-controlled,
of great wealth, lord of treasures, great yogi, fond of the teacher, rich in yoga, destroyer of all disease, shining over the whole earth,
bearer of divine weapons, immeasurable-souled, protector of all, greatly brilliant, bearer of all weapons, giver of desired things, conqueror of enemy cities,
perfected in yoga, huge-bodied, lord of hundreds of great hosts, treasury of all knowledge, the one who makes effort for the success of all —
by the declaration of these hundred and eight names, may the ten forms in the ten quarters, having properly pervaded the ten directions, always protect me.
May all my senses be healthy; may peace always be mine. May the eight forms beginning with Shesha, shining by valour alone,
standing in the corners of fire, Nirriti, wind and Ishana, always protect me. May I have happiness without obstruction, health, invincibility,
destruction of sorrow, freedom from obstacles, increase of progeny, happiness and mercy, attainment of wishes, great welfare, evenness, freedom from disease,
industriousness, what is desired, freedom from death, rise of strength, freedom from fear, fame, beauty, learning, prosperity, great fortune,
no loss of goods, recovery of what is lost, long life, joy of mind, tenderness, what is wished for,
invincibility and great ability — may these be mine through praising Kartavirya, lord of the Haihayas.
This armour of Kartavirya, increasing merit, destroying all sin, destroying all calamities,
making peace in all, secret, destroying all fear, giving victory to men, giving all wealth, auspicious —
whoever hears or reads it obtains all desires. When one sees his wealth such as cattle seized by thieves,
he should chant it seven times at night facing west; in seven nights he regains the lost goods, without doubt.
Chanting it twenty-seven times, facing east, a man may ward off even an enemy army like gods and demons.
In a dispute or terrible quarrel, he who reads it five times gains victory and never defeat.
In all afflictions of disease, he should read three or five times; he is not harmed by disease, death, vetalas, ghouls or ghosts.
Properly chanting it twelve times at night for release from bondage, after three days he is freed from fetters, without doubt.
By this same rule, in all rites of accomplishment, the best mantra-knower accomplishes even the unachievable in a week.
The man who reads this at the time of departure and goes on the road has no fear from wicked thieves, tigers and highwaymen.
Chanting and sprinkling water on the body with cupped hands, he is not troubled by poison, witchcraft, diseases, boils.
Kartavirya, hater of the wicked, son of Kritavirya, strong, thousand-armed, Shatrughna, red-clothed, bow-bearer,
red-scented, red-garlanded, king, giver of desires to one who remembers him: whoever recites these twelve names of Kartavirya,
prosperity comes to him and people are always subject to him. Whoever, O Brahmin, always serves the glorious avatar of the discus,
the discus of the great-souled Vishnu always protects him. This armour, O Brahmin, which I heard from the lord of sages Dattatreya,
has been told to you; wear it, giver of all desires.
Homage, homage to the cause of destroying Meghanada's sacrifice; to the destroyer of the Ashoka grove, giver of victory;
to the son of the Wind, the hero, who goes in the sky's belly; to the cutter of the heads of the forest-guards, the breaker of Lanka's palace;
to him of the colour of blazing gold, bearing a long tail; to the giver of victory to Lakshmana; to Rama's messenger, homage.
To the slayer of Aksha, repeller of Brahma's weapon, destroyer of the wound caused by the great spear at Lakshmana's body,
to the slayer of demons, enemies, spirits, homage, homage; to the one who gladdens the hosts of bears and monkey heroes, homage, homage.
To the destroyer of enemy armies' strength, destroyer of weapons and missiles, homage; to the destroyer of poison, haters and fear, homage, homage.
To the destroyer of the fear of earthly enemies, the sole protector of devotees, the stopper of mantras sent by others,
to the cause of crossing the water on stone, the one who swallowed the disc of the young sun, remover of sorrow,
to the one with nails as weapons, terrible, bearing teeth as weapons; to the bird-like, the corpse-like, the vajra-bodied one, homage.
To the one stationed in each village, the destroyer of ghosts and spirits, to him bearing a mountain as weapon in hand; homage to you, Rama's weapon.
Homage to you, clad in a loincloth, devoted to Rama; to the sun of the south, to the moonrise of the good,
to the destroyer of pain from the wounds of witchcraft, remover of all troubles, the friend giving victory in battle by his master's command,
to the giver of victory to devotees in divine disputes and battle, to the maker of the "kilkila" shout, the maker of dreadful sound,
to the stopper of all fires and diseases, remover of fear, always satisfied especially with forest fruit,
homage to you who built the bridge on stones bound across the great ocean. Thus, O Brahmin, the auspicious armour of Maruti has been told.
It should not be given to just anyone; it should be guarded with effort. One who writes this armour with eight perfumes and wears it
on the neck or right arm has victory at every step. What more need be said? Accomplished by chanting a hundred thousand with respect,
this armour chanted accomplishes even the unachievable.
Hearing that, Shambhu said joyfully to Vishnu: "No one is dearer to me than you, Hari, anywhere.
Not even Parvati is equal to you; there is no difference." Then Gautama bowed to the great God
and said humbly: "O ocean of mercy, immeasurable-souled, by the gods, noon is passing and the time of eating for all has come."
Then Mahadeva, having sipped water, together with Vishnu entered Gautama's house and began to eat.
With jewelled rings, anklets, a silk waist-band, a lightning-like girdle, many necklaces, a neck-ornament, sacred thread and upper garment,
with hanging, swaying jewelled earrings, a fine hair-knot with flowers, an anointing of five fragrances, armlets, bracelets and finger-rings,
Shiva, so adorned, sat on the best seat; and he seated Hari opposite him on an excellent seat.
The two best of gods, Hari and Isha, stood facing each other. Gautama devoutly served food in golden vessels.
Thirty kinds of eatables and fourfold milk-rice, well-cooked dishes and cooked things, two hundred conceived,
and uncooked and mixed ones, thirty likewise; a hundred and a hundred excellent roots and vegetables were arranged.
Twenty-five kinds of side dishes prepared with ghee, sugar and the like, mango, banana, date, pomegranate,
grape, sugar-cane, orange, sweet and ripe heaps of fruit, priyala, kranja, jambu fruit, vikankata fruit —
these and other things having been offered to the Lord, and having given water for sipping, the Brahmin said, "Please eat."
While all were eating, Gautama himself took a fine broad fan and fanned Shiva and Vishnu.
Wishing to make a joke, the Supreme Lord said: "See, Vishnu, how Hanuman, that monkey, eats."
While Hari was looking at the monkey, Maheshvara threw a cake from Vishnu's dish among the sages, as they looked on.
He gave Hanuman his own leavings of milk-rice and the like: "The food left by you, O Lord, is eaten by your own word."

My offering — leaf, flower, fruit and so on — is unfit. Having offered all to me, one should throw it in a well.
naradapuran:78:159	If I do not eat, then surely you are the (superior) one; even if I eat, your grace... in the self-born linga, the moon-stone, the Bana-linga set in the heart,
naradapuran:78:160	eating Shambhu's offering is to be known as equal to the Chandrayana. Now it is time to eat; the distaste in that is from the digression;
naradapuran:78:161	having eaten, I shall tell it; eat it without fear. Then the sage Gautama did the water purification.
He filled the water-pots with water from the tank rubbed with kataka seeds and purified, pots reddish, smooth, fragrant, of fine bodies, washed many times and beautiful.

(A passage describing Gautama preparing perfumed cool drinking water: a new sandy platform on the river bank covered with fine white cloths, pots filled with water set on it, flavoured with jasmine, mixed with sandal and camphor powder, garlands, bakula and patala flowers.)
(Continuing: tuberose flowers in the water, first the water purified; then wrapped with a finer cloth, the mouth of the pipe covered with a fine cloth like moon.)
Placing the water-pots in a shady place with a gentle breeze, fanned with fine fans,
he sprinkled the pipe too with cool, perfumed water. Prepared men, women or kings stood there,
or his daughter with washed limbs and feet, in fine clothes, applying a thick sweet gum of aloe,
on the arms and neck, and a thick paste on the head, a chanter placed, anointed with the five perfumes;
their hair adorned with flowers, they were auspicious and stainless. Women so honoured, bright as saffron in form,
young, lovely in all limbs, richly adorned, with such women or by men he had water given.
At the time of giving, they too wrapped it lightly with fine cloth, or placing it on the left hand and looking at the pot there,
loosening the string tied on it, they then had water given. Thus the blessed sage Gautama arranged it.
When Maheshvara and all the great souls had eaten, with feet and hands washed and hands perfumed,
the God of gods, Maheshvara, seated on a high seat, while the gods and sages sat lower,
arranging in jewelled dishes pieces of areca well scented with incense — not angular, round, large, not fine nor thin —
cleaning white betel leaves, putting in camphor pieces and lime powder, Gautama offered them to Shankara.
When the sage said, "Lord, accept the betel," (Shiva said) "Monkey, take the betel; give me pieces."
The monkey said: "I have no purity, Maheshvara; being an eater of many fruits, how is a monkey pure?"
Hearing that, Virupaksha said to the best of monkeys: "By my word everything becomes pure, by my word poison becomes nectar;
by my word all the Vedas, by my word the gods and others, by my word knowledge of dharma, by my word liberation is spoken;
the Puranas, the scriptures and the Smritis come from my word. Therefore take the betel and give me good pieces."
Hari took betel and areca-pieces with his left hand; then taking leaves he gave pieces to him.
Shiva took the camphor given before and ate it. When the god had taken betel, Parvati from Mount Mandara,
taking the hands of Jaya and Vijaya, came to the sage's house. Bowing at the god's feet, she stood with lowered face.
Lifting her face, the Three-eyed one said: "For your sake, Goddess of gods, I have committed an offence:
that I ate without you, and hear something else, lovely one: that I left you in your own house, I have done a great wrong.
You should forgive, Goddess; give up your anger and look at me." Though thus addressed, she did not speak; she went out with Arundhati.
Knowing her going out, the sage prostrated like a staff. Then Shiva (Parvati) said to him, "Gautama, what do you wish?"
Then Gautama, looking at Goddess Parvati, who smiled, said: "I would be fulfilled if you eat in my house."
Then Shiva said to the Brahmin Gautama, who held folded hands: "I shall eat in your house, Brahmin, with Shankara's permission."
Then, going to Shiva and having received permission, quickly returning, he fed the Goddess, daughter of the mountain, and Arundhati.
Having eaten, Parvati, adorned with perfumes, flowers and all, went to Hara with a thousand maidens as attendants.
Then Shankara said to the Goddess: "Go to Gautama's house; I shall do the twilight worship and come to you."
Having said so, the Goddess went to Gautama's house; all who wished to do twilight worship went out.
At the tank Maheshvara and all the others performed the twilight rites completely. Then Shambhu, facing north, did placing and chanted.
Then the greatly radiant Vishnu said to Maheshvara: "He who is saluted by all and worshipped by all,
to whom offerings are made in all sacrifices — what will you chant, being such? All of us worship you alone with folded hands."
